messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Doc website structure
parts:
Hi all,

In the near future staticdocs should be ready to nicely format all of
ggplot2's documentation, and so I've started to think about how to
host them. I'm currently thinking the easiest way is to serve them
from S3. Github pages are another option, but the documentation is
pretty heavy - there are about 500 example images, and the don't
really need to be in source code control. I also want to keep
multiple versions of the documentation around.

I was thinking of a url like docs.ggplot2.org/0.9.0/...,
docs.ggplot2.org/0.9.1/..., as well as docs.ggplot2.org/latest/

The site would have a robot.txt noindex on everything but latest/ so
that when searching you only every find the latest documentation, but
you have the option of pointing to an older version, if you want. The
challenge is the S3 doesn't support redirects, so latest would have to
be a complete copy of 0.9.1. I'm not sure this is a big deal, except
that there's no way for people to discover the older versions of the
documentation.

Any thoughts?

Hadley

--
Assistant Professor / Dobelman Family Junior Chair
Department of Statistics / Rice University
http://had.co.nz/

I'm sorry I haven't been as involved with the documentation as I originally said I would. If I did, I'd probably know more about the feature roadmap and the documentation updates that you're referring to.
